title: Use a calendar to show the dates that matter in a year and what each one carries.
rule: Draw the year as 12 months in order, each date a square on its day, filled where the law attaches a consequence and open where it states none, with the squares of a busy day stacked. Under it, list every date in order in live text: the day and weekday, what falls due, who acts where the words do not say, and the kind of date in words beside its consequence. Say in a note which dates carry no stated consequence and what can move a date.
use_when: The reader asks which dates in a year carry obligations and which of them carry a consequence, such as the federal budget and tax dates.

use_instead.when: Events across years, with what happened at each
When the parts of one law take effect

text: The year shows at a glance where the dates crowd, and the list gives each one in full. The kind of date in words means no reader has to read a square’s fill to learn whether missing a date carries a consequence.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form calendar: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s94; encode date, event, who, consequence and weekday; labels.none gives the words a consequence opens with where the law states none, labels.tags the two kinds in words, labels.months the year’s month names and labels.key the line over the year. The list is HTML text and the year one drawing beside it (contract R4-3).
